same_explanation_quote: The Medical Man and the Psychologist name it themselves — conjuring — and nothing here supplies a change that would tell it apart from real time travel.
layer_at_fault_line: P6 is marked 'Fixed' though the Psychologist -- a claimant inside the document, not its owner declaring the part off-limits -- merely supplies the patch on the spot; file 33's line 'Fixed - the owner put this part outside the test, and said so' reads as the document's own claimant asserting a part, to a reader marking a document.
quotes: test_remove: 'Drop it and nothing is left calling Duration a dimension.' (P1 row); 'removing it costs the argument nothing. It shows a mind can dwell on the past vividly, not that a body can be relocated in time.' (P4a row). | test_swap: 'swap "gravitation" for any other placeholder obstacle ("friction," "custom," "the usual order of things") and the argument reads exactly the same' (P3 row); 'Swap in a rival account of time's one-wayness (say, an irreversible physical process) and the case for steerable travel does not survive' (P2 row). | test_flip: 'Had the model not vanished, would P1–P4 have had to change? The text suggests not — trust in the Traveller is already a social matter ("too clever to be believed"), so a failed demonstration could just as easily be absorbed as "unfinished."' | test_reverse: 'P1–P4 argue forward, from a definition of dimension to a prediction that travel is possible. P5 is read backward, from an unexplained vanishing to "hence the theory." A vanishing consistent with time-travel is equally consistent with a trick, and nothing offered here tells the two apart.' | test_hunt: '"P2 and P3 already contain most of the conclusion: once "the only difference is which way consciousness moves" is granted, "so movement can be redirected" follows almost from the wording of the analogy, not from anything new.' | test_rival / rivals_built: 'The Medical Man and the Psychologist name it themselves — conjuring — and nothing here supplies a change that would tell it apart from real time travel.' | test_pull / pairs_that_pull: 'P1 is modest (duration exists, call it a dimension) and easy to grant. P3 is far stronger (arbitrary technological control of that dimension). Trust earned on P1's modesty is spent on P3 without new support.' | test_patches: 'introduced exactly when the simpler rival (sleight of hand) is on the table, and tied to no measurement — no stated speed at which the object should become visible again, no reading that would show the patch is wrong rather than merely convenient.' (P6 row); 'attach a gauge to P6 — a stated reading that would show "presentation below the threshold" is being used to swallow a failure rather than describe one.' (section 5). | attributions: 'the Psychologist supplies "presentation below the threshold" on the spot.' (P6, section 2).
